newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Liberals projected to win majority.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Liberals projected to win majority.

text.p: Canada's Liberals were set to be re-elected with a majority government, national television network CTV projected on Monday.

As results flooded in from across the country, the network projected the Liberals would win between 153 and 167 of the 301 seats in Parliament. They needed 151 for a majority government. The Canadian Press news agency also reported that the Liberals were on the brink of a majority.
Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien and Conservative leader Jean Charest were reported elected in their Quebec districts by CBC television.
Also re-elected were Finance Minister Paul Martin in Quebec and Reform leader Preston Manning in Alberta, according to television reports.
The CBC said the Liberals were leading or elected in 152 electoral districts, enough for a parliamentary majority.
The separatist Bloc Quebecois was ahead or elected in 38 seats, Reform 31, the Conservatives 20, New Democrats 15 and others one. The new parliament has 301 seats.
